**Short version:** The three passages are rewritten below with one claim per sentence, literal wording, and a definition at first use. Eight project terms could not be defined from the text alone. They are marked `[DEFINE: …]` in the passages and listed after them.

## Passage 1

```
- Block save. This path handles a run of up to 16 consecutive tokens that lie in one 16-token block. The code transposes the K rows [DEFINE: K row] of the run in registers. It then writes them as whole 64-byte lines (64 bytes is one cache line). Each line takes one store instruction. When the run does not fill the block, the store uses a mask (it writes only the selected bytes of the line). Every decode step (the generation of one new token) produces a run of one token. A run of one token still uses the scatter store (it writes each value to a separate address).
- Sharing. The main thread and the idle main helper threads [DEFINE: main helper thread] share the blocks. Each thread claims its next block from one shared counter. The generated plugin [DEFINE: generated plugin, handwritten plugin] chooses the number of helpers for each pass [DEFINE: pass]. The number is not fixed. In the traced runs it was 7 helpers at tp2 [DEFINE: tp2]. In two cases the calling thread does all the stores. The first case is a caller with a single worker. The handwritten plugins and the unit tests are such callers. The second case is a pass of at most 16 tokens.
```

## Passage 2

```
Where write does worse than read. In some table rows, write keeps less [DEFINE: the quantity that is kept] than read. The first group of rows is two writers in one DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, the Arm block that joins a group of cores and holds their shared cache) at the 160 KiB size (1 KiB is 1024 bytes). The second group is eight writers at every size. In these rows the writers share one path. The limit on that path is either the mesh port of one DSU (the connection from that DSU to the rest of the chip) or the DRAM write ceiling (the highest rate at which main memory accepts writes) [section 8]. One write stream runs at 32 GB/s (gigabytes per second). One read stream runs at 9 to 12 GB/s. So write streams reach the limit with fewer streams than read streams do.
```

## Passage 3

```
Codex (the AI reviewer) gave a closing assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows can answer four questions:

- Does the gain need the prefetchers (hardware that fetches data before the core asks for it)?
- Do the prefetchers place their data in the L3 (the cache shared by one DSU, the Arm DynamIQ Shared Unit that joins a group of cores)?
- Do demand reads (reads that the program itself issues) find their cache lines in the L3?
- Do more requests wait at the home nodes (the mesh nodes that receive the requests sent out by the DSUs)?

The rows alone cannot separate two explanations. Your explanation is that the data is already in the L3 before the core asks for it. The alternative explanation is that the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count [DEFINE: external fetch] with the L3 switched on stays "Insufficient data". Two facts about a counter must first be established on the target machine. The first fact is its source (where its counted events come from). The second fact is its population (which requests it includes).

The bit-6 boot [DEFINE: bit-6 boot] is the only proposed intervention that acts directly on the mechanism in your explanation.
```

## Terms I could not define

Insufficient data: the source documents or the project term list would resolve each one.

| Placeholder | Passage | Note |
|---|---|---|
| K row | 1 | Hypothesis: one key row of the attention key/value cache. |
| main helper thread | 1 | No hint in the text. |
| generated plugin, handwritten plugin | 1 | No hint in the text. |
| pass | 1 | Hypothesis: one model call over a set of tokens. |
| tp2 | 1 | No hint in the text. |
| the quantity that is kept | 2 | The passage does not say what write "keeps". Hypothesis: the share of single-stream throughput. |
| external fetch | 3 | Hypothesis: a fetch that leaves the DSU. |
| bit-6 boot | 3 | The passage names neither the register nor the effect of bit 6. |

## Definitions and readings I supplied

These come from general knowledge or from my reading of the sentence, so please confirm them.

- **Passage 1:**
  - I defined "scatter store" and "decode step".
  - I stated that a 64-byte line is one cache line.
  - I read "keeps the scatter" as "still uses the scatter store".
- **Passage 2:**
  - I defined "DSU", "mesh port", and "DRAM write ceiling".
  - I read "32 GB/s streams" as the rate of each write stream.
  - I read "saturate sooner" as "reach the limit with fewer streams".
- **Passage 3:**
  - I defined "L3", "home nodes", "source", and "population", and I described Codex as the AI reviewer.
  - I read "aim at the L3" as "place their data in the L3".
  - I read "acts on your picture directly" as "acts directly on the mechanism in your explanation".
  - I split the second question into two, which gives four questions instead of three.
- **Passages 2 and 3:** I kept "rows" without a definition, on the assumption that the source documents define the table.
